questions.question: In which Five-Year Plan were Removal of Poverty (Garibi Hatao) and Self-Reliance declared as major plan objectives?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Fifth five-year Plan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan**

 
 
• The Fifth Five-Year Plan of India, which spanned from 1974 to 1979, emphasized the goals of Removal of Poverty (Garibi Hatao) and Self-Reliance.
 
• These objectives were in response to the needs of the time, aiming to address widespread poverty and improve the country's economic independence.
 
• The slogan "Garibi Hatao" became a rallying cry for the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government, symbolizing a commitment to elevating the living standards of India's poor.
 
• The plan also focused on agricultural and rural development, recognising their importance in achieving the twin goals of poverty removal and self-reliance.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Eighth Five-Year Plan
 Focused on the development of human resources including education, health, and employment.
 
 

 2) Seventh Five-Year Plan
 Emphasized policies and programs aimed at food, work, and productivity.
 
 

 4) Sixth Five-Year Plan
 Marked a return to the Five-Year Plan model and focused on poverty alleviation and technological self-reliance.

• This amendment **added a new Part IX to the** Constitution, which is entitled as "**The Panchayats"** and consists of provisions from Articles 243 to 243-O.
 
• It provided a **constitutional status** to the Panchayati Raj institutions for more effective and efficient functioning.
 
• It m**andated the creation of Panchayats at three levels:** village, intermediate, and district levels.
 
• It also **introduced a system of reservations for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in the Panchayat bodies.**

 Article 243-I mandates the State to constitute a Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats.
 
 

 **Elections**
 Article 243-K mandates the State Election Commission to conduct all Panchayat elections.
 
 

 **Duration**
 
 
Panchayats have a term of five years from the date of their first meeting.

__
 
• Article 66

 
 
• Article 66 of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice President.
 
• The Vice President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament.
 
• This election process is indirect, as common citizens do not participate in it.
 
• The Vice President serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• The Vice President may act as the President of India in the absence of the President due to resignation, removal, death, or otherwise.

questions.question: Who was the author of “Mahabhashya”?

__
 
• **Mahabhashya**

 
 
• The "Mahabhashya" is a monumental work on grammar and linguistics.
 
• It was written by Patanjali, an ancient Indian scholar.
 
• This work is a commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi, which is considered the foundational text of Sanskrit grammar.
 
• Patanjali's Mahabhashya not only elucidates Panini's rules but also provides insights into the language and philosophy of the time.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 Details

 Bana was a classical Sanskrit writer known for his work "Harshacharita", a biography of King Harsha.
 
 

 2) Panini
 Panini is renowned for his work "Ashtadhyayi", a treatise on Sanskrit grammar that laid the foundation for classical Sanskrit.
 
 

 3) Patanjali
 Authored "Mahabhashya", a comprehensive commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi, making significant contributions to linguistics.
 
 

 4) Kautilya
 Also known as Chanakya, he was the author of "Arthashastra", an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.

questions.question: In what condition does the body's immune system attack the actual intrinsic factor protein or the cells in your stomach lining that make it?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is**Pernicious anaemia.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pernicious anemia **is a condition in which the body can't make enough healthy red blood cells because it lacks **vitamin B12.**
 
• The **immune system **mistakenly attacks the stomach cells that produce intrinsic factor, a protein necessary** for the absorption of vitamin B12.**
 
• Without intrinsic factor, vitamin B12 can't be absorbed and utilized by the body, leading to a deficiency.
 
• This autoimmune response primarily affects the** gastric mucosa**, where the intrinsic factor is produced.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome
 A neurological disorder typically associated with chronic alcoholism and thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency.
 
 

 2) Hepatic cirrhosis
 A late stage of scarring (fibrosis) of the liver caused by many forms of liver diseases and conditions.
 
 

 4) Hartnup disorder
 A metabolic disorder characterized by impaired absorption of certain amino acids from the diet.

questions.question: Disputes between two or more states comes under the _______ of the Supreme Court.
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is** original jurisdiction.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article-131: Original Jurisdiction**

 
 
• The SC (as a federal court of India) possesses Original jurisdiction to decide the disputes arising between different units of the Indian Federation like:
 
 
• Centre and one or more states; or
 
• Centre & any state(s) on one side and one or more states on the other; or
 
• **Two or more states.**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction - **

 
 
• The Constitution under Article 143 authorises the President to seek the opinion of the Supreme Court in the two categories of matters:
 
• On any question of law or fact of public importance which has arisen or which is likely to arise.
 
• On any dispute arising out of any pre-constitution treaty, agreement, covenant, engagement, sanador other similar instruments.​
 
 
 
• **Appellate Jurisdiction - **
 
 
• ​​The Supreme Court is primarily a court of appeal and hears appeals against the judgements of the lower courts. It enjoys a wide appellate jurisdiction which can be classified under four heads:
 
 

 
• Appeals in constitutional matters
 
• Appeals in civil matters
 
• Appeals in criminal matters
 
• Appeals by special leave​

 
• **Writ Jurisdiction - **

 
 
• The Supreme Court is empowered to issue writs, including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo-warranto and certiorari for the enforcement of the fundamental rights of an aggrieved citizen.
 
• In this regard, the Supreme Court has original jurisdiction in the sense that an aggrieved citizen can go directly to the Supreme Court, not necessarily by way of appeal.
 
• However, the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is not exclusive. The High Courts are also empowered to issue writs for the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights.​

questions.question: Which unsaturated aliphatic hydrocarbon composed of 20 carbon atoms is used to make candles and paraffin wax with solar energy storage capacity?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **Eicosane.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eicosane,** a hydrocarbon with the formula C₂₀H₄₂, is an** unsaturated aliphatic hydrocarbon.**
 
• It is widely used in the **production of candles and paraffin wax** due to its excellent properties for solidification and energy storage.
 
• Its molecular structure, consisting of 20 carbon atoms, makes it suitable for solar energy storage applications, where it can absorb, store, and release solar energy.
 
• The use of eicosane in these applications is because of its phase change properties, which are highly efficient for thermal energy storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 1) Octane
 Octane, or C8H18, is a component of gasoline and has 8 carbon atoms. It is known for its role in the octane rating of fuel.
 
 

 2) Eicosane
 Eicosane, or C20H42, is used in candles, paraffin wax, and for solar energy storage due to its phase change properties.
 
 

 3) Nonane
 Nonane, or C9H20, is a hydrocarbon with 9 carbon atoms, primarily used as a solvent or in the production of plastics.
 
 

 4) Triacontane
 Triacontane, or C30H62, is a hydrocarbon with 30 carbon atoms, used in waxes, lubricants, and as a waterproofing agent.

questions.question: Which of the following industries are engaged in the reproduction and multiplication of certain spices of plants and animals with the object of sale?

__
 
• The **Genetic industry** is involved in the reproduction and multiplication of plant and animal species for commercial purposes.
 
• It **plays a crucial role** in biotechnology and agriculture, focusing on genetic modification and selective breeding.
 
• These** industries produce **genetically modified crops, livestock, and other organisms that offer higher yields and are sometimes resistant to pests and diseases.
 
• They **contribute significantly to food security, medical research, and environmental sustainability**.
 
• The industry's **practices include **cloning, gene editing, and the use of recombinant DNA technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Key Term
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Biotechnology**
 A field of science that involves the use of living organisms, systems, or processes in manufacturing and service industries.
 
 

 **Genetic Modification (GM)**
 The manipulation of an organism's genes using biotechnology to create a genetically modified organism (GMO) with new traits.
 
 

 **Selective Breeding**
 The process of breeding plants and animals for particular genetic traits to improve species.
 
 

 **Cloning**
 The process of creating genetically identical copies of biological matter, including genes, cells, and organisms.
 
 

 **Recombinant DNA Technology**
 A technology that involves combining DNA from two different sources to create a new genetic combination.

• **The administrative system of the Vijayanagar Empir**e was highly efficient in collecting taxes and revenues from the land, which were then used for the empire's development and expansion.

 Import duties from foreign trade were significant but secondary to the income generated from land revenue.

• Na (Sodium) is not an alkaline earth metal; instead, it is an alkali metal, which belongs to Group 1 of the periodic table.
 
• Mg (Magnesium), Ca (Calcium), and Be (Beryllium) are all part of Group 2, making them alkaline earth metals.

 Details

 Sodium (Na) is **an alkali metal**, not an alkaline earth metal. It has **a single electron in its outermost shell**.
 
 

 2) Mg
 Magnesium (Mg) is an alkaline earth metal with **two electrons in its outer shell**, making it highly reactive.
 
 

 3) Ca
 Calcium (Ca) is another alkaline earth metal, essential for living organisms, especially in bone formation.

questions.question:
Which of the following reasons can be attributed to the excessive pressure on agricultural land in India?

(a) right of inheritance

(b) size of unprofitable land holding

(c) division of land

d) multiple cropping
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ Option 4__.

__
 
• **Right of inheritance** 

 
 
• When land is **divided **among legal heirs, it leads to smaller landholdings. Hence, (a) is correct. 
 
 
 
• **Uneconomic size of landholdings**
 
 
• Small landholdings are **not viable **for profitable farming. Hence, (b) is correct. 
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation of land**: 
 
 
• **Division of land into small**, scattered plots makes it difficult to cultivate efficiently. 
 
• These factors contribute to the **excessive pressure **on agricultural land in India. Hence, (c) is correct.
 
 
 
• **Multiple cropping**
 
 
• **More than one crop grown **on a piece of land during the year is known as multiple cropping.
 
• It is the most common way of **increasing production **on a given piece of land.
 
• All land is cultivated and **no ground is left idle **at any time during the year.Hence, (d) is incorrect.
